title: Benny Benjamin - Wikipedia
notes: William Benjamin Jr., 'Papa Zita'; born 25 July 1925 in Birmingham, Alabama (some sources give 15 July); died 20 April 1969 in Detroit, aged 43, of a stroke. Learned the drums in the style of the 1940s big bands; influenced by Buddy Rich and Tito Puente. Motown's first studio drummer, from 1958; a Funk Brother. Berry Gordy and James Jamerson reportedly refused to work on sessions unless he was the drummer; the Beatles singled out his drumming when they met Gordy in Britain. Lists Money, Shop Around, Do You Love Me, Get Ready, My Girl, I Can't Help Myself, Uptight ('some sources credit Richard "Pistol" Allen'), You Can't Hurry Love, I Heard It Through the Grapevine (Gladys Knight) and Going to a Go-Go. By the late 1960s he 'struggled with drug and alcohol addiction', and Uriel Jones and Pistol Allen recorded more of the drum tracks. A studio set of Ludwig, Slingerland, Rogers and Gretsch parts, likely Zildjian cymbals. Rock and Roll Hall of Fame 2003; Rolling Stone's eleventh greatest drummer, 2016.

title: DRUM! Magazine: Sunday Sounds: Benny Benjamin's 'Supreme' Motown Sound (Anna Pulley, 28 October 2018)
notes: On the Supremes' My World Is Empty Without You (1965), 'the dynamic drumming of popular session man Benny Benjamin'. Berry Gordy: 'He had a pulse, a steadiness, that kept the tempo better than a metronome.' Stevie Wonder: 'I learned from just listening to him. Man, he was one of the major forces in the Motown sound.' No transcription.

title: Modern Drummer: Uriel Jones, Architect of the Motown Sound (interview by Drew Shultz; August 2009 issue, online 13 June 2011)
notes: Jones credits Benjamin with the Motown pickups, the fills 'sampled more than any drum pickups ever', made to fit between his drums and Jamerson's bass; he modelled his own playing on Benjamin's, and after Benjamin left the sessions was used on most tunes for having cloned his approach. A drummer quoted in it (Rountree) says Benjamin was 'a thinker', kept the focus on the singers, 'showed me that you don't have to be wild to play', and that his simple time made the occasional lick stand out: 'he makes it breathe'.

title: Modern Drummer: The Drummers of Motown (Zoro and Allan Slutsky, July 1999; online as Secrets of Motown, 18 June 2009)
notes: In the early years Benjamin or Pistol Allen dragged his own kit down the studio steps; by late 1963 Motown had a permanent, second-hand set of mixed makes in Studio A. Uriel Jones: no expensive set stayed in the studio because Benny 'would sneak in from time to time and pawn them'; once he convinced the night watchman the set was his. The vibist Jack Brokensha offered to drum until Benny got there.

title: Loudlands Music: The Uncredited Drummers of Motown: The Funk Brothers (Josh Merhar)
notes: Undated blog. Benjamin 'would frequently use brushes on recordings'; his 'timekeeping abilities and control of dynamics'; told Pistol Allen to 'leave the jazz drumming at home, hold down simple beats, and to keep his mouth shut'; notorious for lateness and elaborate excuses; alcoholism and heroin addiction; Allen and Jones took over his duties. Read as a summary of the usual accounts.

title: Drummerszone: Benny 'Papa Zita' Benjamin
notes: The nickname: caught asleep at his kit by a producer, he woke drumming and calling 'Papa-zita, papa-zita'. Primary drummer on the Miracles' Doin' Mickey's Monkey (1963), a 'Bo Diddley-style' groove on its title track. Unsourced.

title: YouTube: MOTOWN's Benny Benjamin drumming style (5SShCxpUc4M)
notes: A drummer's lesson on his grooves; it opens with archive photographs. 0:26–0:34: Benjamin smiling over a cymbal, close-cut hair, a thin moustache, a pale flecked sport coat over a white shirt open at the neck. The one photograph of him at the kit found; the likeness is drawn from it.

title: Money (That's What I Want) - Wikipedia
notes: Barrett Strong; Tamla, August 1959, licensed to Anna in 1960 and distributed by Chess. From a spontaneous session in Hitsville's Studio A. Personnel: Strong, vocals; Berry Gordy, piano; 'Benny Benjamin – drums'; Eugene Grew, guitar; Brian Holland, tambourine; the bassist unknown.

title: Do You Love Me (The Contours song) - Wikipedia
notes: Gordy, 1962; produced by Berry Gordy at Hitsville's Studio A. The backing included 'Benny Benjamin on drums'; the personnel list credits the Funk Brothers.

title: My Girl (The Temptations song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded 25 September and 10 and 17 November 1964 at Hitsville; released 21 December 1964 on Gordy; produced by Smokey Robinson and Ronald White. Personnel: 'Benny Benjamin – drums'.

title: I Can't Help Myself (Sugar Pie Honey Bunch) - Wikipedia
notes: The Four Tops; recorded 1965 at Hitsville's Studio A; released 23 April 1965 on Motown. Personnel: 'Drums by Benny Benjamin', James Jamerson on bass.

title: Uptight (Everything's Alright) - Wikipedia
notes: Stevie Wonder; Tamla, 22 November 1965; No. 3 pop, No. 1 R&B for five weeks. Personnel: 'Benny Benjamin – drums'. (Benjamin's own article notes that some sources credit Pistol Allen.)

title: Get Ready (The Temptations song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded 5, 9 and 29 December 1965 at Hitsville's Studio A; released 7 February 1966. 'A prominent rhythm provided by Motown drummer Benny Benjamin.'

title: Going to a Go-Go (song) - Wikipedia
notes: The Miracles; recorded 17 August 1965 at Hitsville; released 6 December 1965. Personnel: 'Benny Benjamin – drums'.

title: You Can't Hurry Love - Wikipedia
notes: The Supremes; recorded 11 June and 5 July 1966 at Hitsville's Studio A; released 25 July 1966. Personnel: 'Benny Benjamin – drums'.

title: Baby Love - Wikipedia
notes: The Supremes, 17 September 1964: drums by Richard 'Pistol' Allen, footstomps by Mike Valvano. Read to rule it out: not Benjamin's.
